name: Pause Squat
description: The pause squat is a barbell back squat variation where the lifter pauses motionless at the bottom of the movement for a prescribed duration, typically two to five seconds, before driving back to the top. The pause eliminates the stretch-shortening reflex that assists normal squatting, forcing the muscles to generate force from a dead stop. This builds positional strength, reinforces technique, and identifies mobility or stability weaknesses.

execution.starting_position: Same setup as a standard barbell back squat: bar on upper traps, feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
execution.setup_instructions: Set up identically to a back squat. Use 70–85% of your normal squat working weight for 2-second pauses. Reduce weight further for longer pauses.
steps: Step 1: Unrack the bar and set up as for a back squat. Take a deep breath and brace.
Step 2: Descend under control to full depth — hips at or below parallel.
Step 3: Hold the bottom position completely still for the prescribed time (2–5 seconds). Do not relax. Actively maintain tension throughout: knees out, chest up, core braced.
Step 4: Without any counter-movement, drive explosively through the floor to return to standing.
Step 5: Exhale at the top, reset, and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Hold breath through the pause and ascent. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Relaxing the core, knees, or torso position during the pause
Rising onto the toes at the bottom
Using too much weight, which turns the pause into a brief wobble
safety_considerations: Use safety bars — a failed pause squat has less momentum to rescue than a normal squat
Reduce load by 15–25% compared to your regular squat weight
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth (hips at or below parallel). The pause must be at the deepest position, not above parallel.
coaching_cues: Stay tight during the pause — don't let anything relax
Drive the knees out actively while holding the bottom
Explode up — don't grind up slowly
